overview: Nekoware v1's Criticals is a byte-for-byte port of the Memeware 7.3 module whose registered modes ('Edit', 'Packet') match none of the handler branches. The PacketOutEvent handler only responds to the mode names 'Mineplex', 'Cubecraft' and 'GroundSpoof', and isMode compares with equalsIgnoreCase, so no selection can ever reach a branch: the module compiles, registers, and does nothing. The dead code still documents the intended behavior - an every-other-tick onGround=false flip with a silent 1.02E-9 C04 lift (Mineplex), a 0.1232225/1.0554E-9/0 three-packet trail behind each C02 attack (Cubecraft), and a swing-gated decaying 0.001 y-lift (GroundSpoof).

sections.p: The file is structurally identical to its Memeware parent: a Timer (critTimer) and a groundSpoofDist double (0.001, reset by onEnable and onDisable), a PacketOutEvent handler that mutates outgoing C03 packets in place and uses PacketUtil.sendPacketSilent for injected packets, and an UpdateEvent handler that edits the motion event's y and onGround fields. The one difference is the mode list: the constructor registers 'Edit' and 'Packet' instead of Memeware's 'Ground Spoof', 'Packet', 'Mineplex'. Every isMode() test in both handlers targets names that are no longer registered, so all three behavior branches are unreachable. The module is a template whose handlers were never rewired to the new mode names - a copy-paste port that lost its trigger conditions.

The latent offsets are exactly Memeware's. The Mineplex branch would force onGround false on every C03 on even ticks while isCollidedVertically, and would inject a silent C04 at y + 1.02E-9 with onGround false for position packets - a sub-0.03-min-move lift the server ignores as a coordinate but accepts as a flag. The Cubecraft branch would trail each C02 attack (at 320ms intervals) with C04 y + 0.1232225 off-ground, C04 y + 1.0554E-9 off-ground, and C04 y onGround true. The GroundSpoof branch would raise the update y by groundSpoofDist - 0.001 decaying 1E-11 per use, resetting from below 0.0001 - while a swing is in progress and the player is collided vertically. None of it can fire under the registered modes, so the module has no observable timing behavior at all.

Because the handlers are unreachable, the module has no interaction with attacks: a C02 sent by Nekoware's Aura passes through the PacketOutEvent handler unmodified, the UpdateEvent edits nothing, and groundSpoofDist only changes inside onEnable/onDisable. The design intent, copied from the parent, was to make attacks land while the server believed the player airborne - the Mineplex branch flips the flag for every packet in the attack window, the Cubecraft branch re-positions after the C02, and the GroundSpoof branch ties the lift to swings - but the mode-name mismatch severs every path. Any future fix that renames a registered mode to one of the tested strings ('Mineplex', 'Cubecraft' or 'GroundSpoof') would activate the corresponding latent behavior unchanged.

files.label: Criticals.java (module logic)
files.explanation: The file is a verbatim port of Memeware 7.3's Criticals with the mode registration changed and the handlers untouched. The constructor (line 20) registers 'Edit' and 'Packet' (line 22), but the PacketOutEvent handler (line 25) tests isMode('Mineplex') (line 30), isMode('Cubecraft') (line 41) and isMode('GroundSpoof') (line 64), and Module.isMode does an equalsIgnoreCase comparison against the registered value - so no branch can ever match. The dead branches are the Memeware patterns: the Mineplex branch flips onGround to false on even ticks and injects a silent C04 at y + 1.02E-9 via PacketUtil.sendPacketSilent; the Cubecraft branch appends C04 y + 0.1232225 (false), C04 y + 1.0554E-9 (false) and C04 y (true) behind each C02 attack when the 320ms Timer allows; the GroundSpoof branch in the UpdateEvent handler (line 59) would lift y by groundSpoofDist (0.001, decaying 1E-11, reset below 0.0001) and claim off-ground per swing. onEnable/onDisable (lines 71-79) only reset groundSpoofDist, so enabling the module has no other effect.

files.label: PacketUtil.java (send paths)
files.explanation: Identical to the Memeware original apart from the package name. sendPacketSilent calls mc.getNetHandler().getNetworkManager().sendPacket(packet) directly, bypassing the send queue and the event bus - the path the latent Mineplex branch would use to write its 1.02E-9 C04 immediately. sendPacket routes through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue, the path the latent Cubecraft branch would use to append its three C04s behind the C02. The distinction matters because the dead code's wire ordering depends entirely on which of the two paths each packet takes.

countering.label: Criticals (combat-side vertical check)
countering.explanation: The latent patterns are exactly what Arc v2's Criticals check is built to catch. On every attack it compares Arc's physics-derived ground state (data.isOnGround(), maintained by Arc's own MovingListener from world collision) against the vertical speed of the current move: on the ground with vertical speed below 0.37, the hit is 'critical while onGround'. The latent Cubecraft lift of 0.1232225 is a vertical speed of 0.12, and the Mineplex pattern attacks with a near-zero vertical speed while claiming off-ground - both violate on the first attack, because Arc's ground state is world-derived and immune to the packet onGround flips the module would send.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical movement envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's vertical envelope (vDistRel, invoked at line 212) accepts only zero-y-on-ground, real jumps, step-ups and riptide. The latent Cubecraft lift of 0.1232225 from a standing position matches none of them, producing a yDistanceAboveLimit of ~0.12 that feeds the (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 violation (line 233) and its set-back. The sub-min-move lifts (1.02E-9 and the 0.001 decay band) sit below the 0.03 move threshold the envelope even sees, which is the design intent of those constants; the combat-side vertical checks cover that residue, as with the Memeware original.

countering.label: SmallHop (mini-jump detection)
countering.explanation: SmallHop exists to catch exactly these mini-jumps - its own docstring says small jumps can be exploited 'to bypass other checks such as speed and criticals'. The latent Cubecraft hop of 0.1232225 is a textbook match: wasOnGround, 0 < deltaY < 0.4, prevDeltaY <= 0, no accepted knockback or slime bounce, no ladder/vine or adjacent solid, and a destination that AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally (0.001 tolerance) reports as air - punish and rubberband. The 1.02E-9 and decaying-0.001 lifts stay inside the ground tolerance and are the mode's intended evasion, which is why the family of checks is layered: envelope for the visible offsets, ground-truth tolerance for the sub-pixel residue.

countering.label: fight.Critical (critical-hit validation)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight.Critical is the dedicated check for the class of cheat this module's dead code implements. Its divergence rule flags any crit whose server-side fallDistance is not corroborated by NCP's own noFallFallDistance (tracked from ray-traced ground) while the player is judged on-ground, and its jump-phase rule flags crits delivered in the first phases of a jump before the full lift-off arc. For the latent Cubecraft ordering - C04s enqueued behind the C02 - the attack also simply arrives with zero fall distance and registers no crit at all, since the server evaluates the hit before the trailing lift; the pattern only survives when its packets race ahead of the attack, which is precisely the condition the divergence rule is designed to detect.
